purpose: Machine-checkable map of public products and onboarding surfaces. Every entry must be explained in both zero-to-first-result guides.

surfaces.name: AI Social Media Toolkit
surfaces.what: The umbrella repository that connects prompts, assistant blueprints, Agent Skills, MCP examples, creator tools, automation and trust evidence.
surfaces.why: Use one public place to discover the smallest AI layer that solves a creator or workflow job without pretending every job needs an autonomous agent.
surfaces.who: Creators, AI builders, social-media specialists and small teams who want inspectable reusable workflows.
surfaces.first_step: Run python tools/first_run_check.py from a cloned/downloaded repository, or use the live Creator Frame Studio if you do not want a terminal.
surfaces.expected_result: A PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED first-run result plus a clear next path.
surfaces.verify: FIRST-RUN CHECK: PASS and the documented output for the chosen path.
surfaces.limitations: A local pass is not universal host compatibility, independent adoption, virality or revenue proof.

surfaces.name: Creator Context Builder
surfaces.what: Builds one reusable creator/brand context with facts, preferences, observed style patterns and hypotheses kept separate.
surfaces.why: Stops users from repeating the same briefing and reduces brand-voice drift across downstream skills.
surfaces.who: Anyone using several personalized creator workflows or working with changing metrics/brand rules.
surfaces.first_step: Install only creator-context-builder or open its SKILL.md, then provide current facts plus approved writing/content samples.
surfaces.expected_result: A reusable creator-context.md file, stale/recheck list and up to three next-skill recommendations.
surfaces.verify: Facts are labeled VERIFIED, preferences PREFERENCE, sample-derived patterns OBSERVED and uncertain interpretations HYPOTHESIS.
surfaces.limitations: It must not infer sensitive traits, store secrets or treat old metrics as current.

surfaces.name: Creator Ops
surfaces.what: Routes an end-to-end creator job to the minimum relevant specialized workflows.
surfaces.why: Prevents one giant generic answer from replacing proper research, production and review stages.
surfaces.who: Users who know the outcome they want but are unsure which skill/tool should handle it.
surfaces.first_step: State the objective, platform, evidence, constraints and definition of success.
surfaces.expected_result: An ordered workflow, correct sub-skill routing, review gate and measurement step.
surfaces.verify: The output separates evidence, decision, production and review instead of jumping directly to content.
surfaces.limitations: It is an orchestrator, not proof that any platform API or external account is connected.

surfaces.name: Creator Frame Studio
surfaces.what: Frames one visual across social aspect ratios, adds editable text and runs deterministic preflight checks.
surfaces.why: Reduces rework when a visual breaks while moving between 4:5, 9:16, 2:3 and 16:9 formats.
surfaces.who: Creators and social-media teams who need fast visual adaptation without uploading the source image to a service.
surfaces.first_step: Open the live demo or download the offline ZIP, add a non-sensitive image and switch formats.
surfaces.expected_result: A reviewed export for the selected format plus visible preflight status.
surfaces.verify: The app loads locally, CSP blocks network connections and exported framing matches the selected profile.
surfaces.limitations: It is not an AI image generator, publishing service or guarantee that a platform UI will never change.

surfaces.name: MCP Permission Inspector
surfaces.what: Reviews an MCP client configuration before first connection and surfaces permission/config risk signals.
surfaces.why: Makes hidden first-connect assumptions visible before a server is launched.
surfaces.who: Developers and users adding MCP servers to a client configuration.
surfaces.first_step: Use a sanitized test config first and review every finding before using a real config.
surfaces.expected_result: A local review of declared server/config behavior and items that need human attention.
surfaces.verify: No server is launched and no runtime-safety claim is made.
surfaces.limitations: Static configuration review cannot detect remote/runtime behavior drift after installation.

surfaces.name: AI Workbench MCP
surfaces.what: Exposes a local catalog through three read-only MCP tools: list_prompts, render_prompt and get_assistant.
surfaces.why: Provides a deliberately small MCP boundary that is easy to inspect, test and connect to a host.
surfaces.who: Users who want reusable prompt/assistant artifacts through MCP without network, shell, account or file-write access.
surfaces.first_step: Install the exact PyPI alpha, run --doctor, then configure the documented host.
surfaces.expected_result: Doctor PASS, three tools discovered and successful local tool invocation.
surfaces.verify: doctor -> handshake -> host discovery -> tool invocation -> expected output.
surfaces.limitations: A doctor pass does not prove every MCP host works; host compatibility must be verified separately.

surfaces.name: Agent Skill Safety Auditor
surfaces.what: Scans an Agent Skill folder for risky execution, network, credential, environment and lifecycle patterns before installation.
surfaces.why: Agent Skills are supply-chain inputs; a readable SKILL.md can still trigger powerful scripts or permissions.
surfaces.who: Anyone reviewing third-party Agent Skills before installing or reusing them.
surfaces.first_step: Clone the repo, install locally, then run skill-audit against a test/third-party skill folder.
surfaces.expected_result: LOW/MODERATE/HIGH findings with file/line evidence for manual review.
surfaces.verify: The scanner stays offline and findings point to concrete evidence instead of declaring a project malicious.
surfaces.limitations: Static scanning cannot prove runtime safety or detect a remote service changing behavior after install.

surfaces.name: Creator Signal Lab
surfaces.what: Two dependency-free CSV tools rank content opportunities and detect posts that are outliers against a local baseline.
surfaces.why: Makes scoring formulas and assumptions inspectable instead of hiding them behind a black-box virality score.
surfaces.who: Creators/strategists with explicit CSV inputs who want prioritization and outlier analysis.
surfaces.first_step: Run the bundled synthetic examples before using your own CSV.
surfaces.expected_result: Ranked CSV/text output with explainable score components.
surfaces.verify: Bundled sample produces the documented result and malformed inputs fail loudly.
surfaces.limitations: No scraping, no live analytics connector, no AI model and no probability/virality guarantee.

surfaces.name: Prompt Library
surfaces.what: Reusable prompts with required inputs, expected outputs, quality checks, examples and troubleshooting.
surfaces.why: Turns one-off prompts into inspectable reusable jobs.
surfaces.who: Users who need a repeatable AI task but do not need an Agent Skill or MCP server.
surfaces.first_step: Pick one job in prompts/README.md and fill only the documented inputs.
surfaces.expected_result: A task-specific instruction with an explicit quality gate.
surfaces.verify: The output can be checked against the prompt's expected-output and QA sections.
surfaces.limitations: A prompt is not an autonomous agent and does not create external account access.

surfaces.name: Assistant Blueprints
surfaces.what: Reusable role/instruction packages that can be adapted to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok or portable Agent Skill formats.
surfaces.why: Keeps one job definition portable instead of rewriting the same assistant from scratch for every provider.
surfaces.who: Users who repeat the same multi-step AI job in a custom assistant/project/gem.
surfaces.first_step: Choose a blueprint, export it for a target host and review provider-specific limitations.
surfaces.verify: The same underlying job remains recognizable across provider exports.
surfaces.limitations: Exporting text does not automatically create/publish/configure an assistant account.

surfaces.name: Agent Skills
surfaces.what: Markdown-based reusable procedures that compatible AI agents can load for specific jobs.
surfaces.why: Moves repeatable process knowledge closer to the agent without turning every workflow into custom code.
surfaces.who: Users of compatible Agent Skills runtimes such as supported Codex/Claude/Cursor/Gemini-style environments.
surfaces.first_step: List skills, install one relevant skill, then ask the documented first request.
surfaces.expected_result: The agent applies the installed procedure and returns the defined artifact.
surfaces.verify: Confirm the loaded path, use a synthetic input first and compare with the documented contract.
surfaces.limitations: Installation does not grant external accounts or prove every runtime behaves identically.

surfaces.name: Automation Recipes and GitHub Automations
surfaces.what: Patterns and GitHub Actions for recurring research, validation, monitoring and bounded recovery.
surfaces.why: Some jobs are valuable because they repeat, not because one AI answer is clever.
surfaces.who: Maintainers who understand the underlying manual workflow and want repeatable execution.
surfaces.first_step: Run the manual workflow once, identify permissions and failure conditions, then choose the narrow recipe.
surfaces.expected_result: A repeatable job with explicit trigger, permissions, output, read-back and stop conditions.
surfaces.verify: Check actual run history and output freshness; configured schedules are not proof a run succeeded.
surfaces.limitations: Automation must not silently expand permissions, publish without authorization or turn weak signals into facts.

surfaces.name: Rewrite Fact Guard
surfaces.what: Compares an original and rewritten draft for changed number-like tokens, common units, literal URLs and exact protected phrases.
surfaces.why: Catches mechanical factual-token drift after rewriting without sending the drafts to an AI model or external API.
surfaces.who: Creators, editors and small teams who have both before/after text and want a local review aid before publication.
surfaces.first_step: Run python skills/brand-voice-humanizer/scripts/fact_guard.py with the bundled before.txt and after-good.txt examples plus --lock "garanti değildir".
surfaces.expected_result: The unchanged synthetic example returns NO_TRACKED_CHANGE with exit code 0; the changed synthetic example returns REVIEW_REQUIRED with exit code 1 and documented findings.
surfaces.verify: Run both bundled examples and compare the status, finding count and exit code with skills/brand-voice-humanizer/README.md.
surfaces.limitations: It is lexical drift detection, not semantic fact checking, AI-authorship detection, legal review or a publication guarantee. Unchanged tokens can still have changed associations and unprotected qualifiers can change undetected.
